# Module 1: Foundations of Belief (Level 1: Ages 6-8)

| Curriculum Metadata | Details |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Target Age Group** | Level 1: Ages 6-8 (Primary Stage 1) |
| **Estimated Study Time** | 45 minutes |
| **Prerequisites** | None (Foundational level) |
| **Surah Anchor / Tafsir** | Surah Al-Ikhlas (112:1-4) & Surah Al-Fatihah (1:1-7) |
| **Tajweed Rule** | Clear Pronunciation (Isti'adhah and Basmalah) |
| **Classical Text Anchor** | 'Aqidat al-'Awamm (Lines 1-5) & Matn Ibn 'Ashir |
| **Hadith Anchor (Nawawi 40)** | Hadith 2: The Hadith of Jibril (Islam and Iman) |

---

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
1. Explain that Allah is Al-Khaliq (The Creator) Who made everything in the heavens and the earth.
2. State the golden promise of faith: the Shahaadah (testimony of faith).
3. Name the three judgements of character and list the Five Pillars of Islam.
4. Name the angels of pure light (Jibril, Mika'il, and the guardian angels).
5. Recite Surah Al-Ikhlas with understanding and apply daily Sunnah manners.

---

## Section 1: Welcome to the Wonder of Creation
Have you ever looked up at the deep blue sky, watched a butterfly flutter between flowers, or listened to the gentle rain tapping on your window?

When you see a colorful painting, you know an artist painted it. When you taste fresh, warm bread, you know a baker prepared it. When we look at this vast, orderly world, our hearts know that Allah is its Maker and Sustainer.

Allah is Al-Khaliq (The Creator). He made the sun to give us warm light, the tall trees to produce sweet fruit, and the ocean for creatures of all shapes. He gave each of us a beating heart, bright eyes, two ears, and a caring family. Whenever we see beauty in nature, our hearts remember Allah and we say: **SubhanAllah** (Glory be to Allah).

---

## Section 2: The Golden Promise of Faith (Tawheed & Shahaadah)
The most precious treasure in our hearts is **Tawheed** (تَوْحِيد). Tawheed means knowing and declaring that Allah is One, Unique, and without partner.

* Allah has no partners, no parents, and no children.
* He never grows tired, He never sleeps, and He never needs food or drink.
* He created everything out of His infinite Wisdom and Mercy.

Every day, Muslims declare their faith through the golden words of the Shahaadah:

> **أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱللَّٰهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ ٱللَّٰهِ**  
> *"Ash-hadu an la ilaha illa Allah, wa ash-hadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah"*  
> (I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah!)

### The Golden Rule of Our Creed:
The great Sunni scholars of creed taught us a golden guiding rule:
> *"Whatever comes to your mind or imagination, Allah is completely different from that!"* (Attributed to Dhu al-Nun al-Misri and Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal; cited by al-Qushayri).

Allah is greater, more majestic, and more pure than anything a human being can imagine or draw. We never draw pictures or imagine shapes of Allah, because nothing in creation is like Him (Surah Ash-Shura 42:11).

---

## Section 3: Allah's Helpers: The Angels of Pure Light
Allah created the noble **Angels** (*Mala'ikah*) from pure light (*Nur*). They love Allah, carry out His commands perfectly, and never disobey.

| Angel | Noble Duty |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Angel Jibril (Gabriel)** | The leader of the angels who brought the Qur'an and revelation to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and all the prophets. |
| **Angel Mika'il (Michael)** | Entrusted by Allah with the rainfall that causes plants and crops to grow. |
| **Guardian Angels (Al-Kiram al-Katibin)** | Stay near us, protect us by Allah's leave, and write down our good deeds. |

When you say *"Bismillah"*, smile at your parents, or share your toys with your sibling, the angels record your good deeds in your book of blessings.

---

## Section 4: The Five Pillars of Islam
Our religion of Islam is like a strong building supported by **Five Pillars**:

1. **The Shahaadah**: Believing with full conviction that Allah is One and Muhammad is His Messenger ﷺ.
2. **Salah (Prayer)**: Speaking directly to Allah in prayer five times every day with clean clothes and a focused heart.
3. **Zakah (Giving)**: Sharing a portion of savings with families in need once every year.
4. **Sawm (Fasting)**: Abstaining from food and drink during daylight hours in the blessed month of Ramadan.
5. **Hajj (Pilgrimage)**: Journeying to the sacred Ka'bah in Makkah once in a lifetime for those who are able.

---

## Section 5: Curriculum Anchors in Practice

### 5.1 Qur'an and Tafsir Anchor: Surah Al-Ikhlas (112:1-4)
> **بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ**  
> **قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ ۝ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ ۝ لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ ۝ وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ**  
> *Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad. Allahus-Samad. Lam yalid wa lam yulad. Wa lam yakun lahu kufuwan ahad.*  
> "Say: He is Allah, the One! Allah, the Eternal Refuge! He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent." (Surah Al-Ikhlas 112:1-4)

**Tafsir Insights**: This short chapter teaches us pure Tawheed. The word *Al-Ahad* means Allah is perfectly One without parts or partners. *Al-Samad* means every created thing depends on Allah, while Allah needs nothing from anyone.

### 5.2 Tajwid Rule in Action: Clear Pronunciation of Basmalah
When reading the Qur'an, we begin with:
* **Al-Isti'adhah**: *A'udhu billahi min ash-shaytan ir-rajim* (seeking refuge with Allah from the expelled devil).
* **Al-Basmalah**: *Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim* (in the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful).
* **Pronunciation Tip**: Pronounce each Arabic letter gently and clearly from its correct exit point (*Makhraj*) without rushing.

### 5.3 Classical Text Anchor: 'Aqidat al-'Awamm
> "We begin with the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful, and all praise belongs to Allah, the Eternal Who has no beginning." ('Aqidat al-'Awamm, Lines 1-2).

**Explanation**: Classical teachers across generations have started their lessons with these lines to remind young students that all blessings come from Allah.

### 5.4 Prophetic Hadith Anchor: Hadith Jibril
> "Islam is that you bear witness that there is no god worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, that you establish prayer, give Zakah, fast Ramadan, and make the pilgrimage to the House if you are able." (Sahih Muslim 8, Sahih; 40 Hadith Nawawi, Hadith 2)

**Living the Hadith**: Practice your daily prayers on time and make it a habit to say *Bismillah* before eating and *Alhamdulillah* after finishing.

---

## Summary and Key Takeaways
* Allah is Al-Khaliq, the Creator of the heavens, the earth, and everything within them.
* Tawheed means knowing that Allah is One, unique, and does not resemble anything in creation.
* Islam is built upon Five Pillars: Shahaadah, Salah, Zakah, Sawm, and Hajj.
* The angels are created from light and always obey Allah's commands.

(A) Angel Mika'il
(B) Angel Israfil
(C) Angel Malik
(D) Angel Jibril

**5. When you see a beautiful flower or an amazing sunset, what praise should you say?**
(A) SubhanAllah (Glory be to Allah)
(B) Astaghfirullah (I seek forgiveness from Allah)
(C) JazakAllahu Khayran (May Allah reward you with good)
(D) Bismillah (In the name of Allah)

Vocabulary Bank: Creator, One, Light, Five

* SubhanAllah ─── Glory be to Allah

# Module 1: Foundations of Belief (Level 2: Ages 8-10)

| Curriculum Metadata | Details |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Target Age Group** | Level 2: Ages 8-10 (Primary Stage 2) |
| **Estimated Study Time** | 50 minutes |
| **Prerequisites** | Level 1 Foundations of Belief |
| **Surah Anchor / Tafsir** | Surah Al-Ikhlas (112:1-4) & Surah Al-A'la (87:1-5) |
| **Tajweed Rule** | Ghunnah & Heavy Letters (Huruf al-Isti'la') |
| **Classical Text Anchor** | Matn al-'Ashmawiyyah & Al-Risalah of Ibn Abi Zayd |
| **Hadith Anchor (Nawawi 40)** | Hadith 2: The Hadith of Jibril (Iman and Ihsan) |

---

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
1. Explain the narrative context and lessons of the Hadith of Jibril recorded in Sahih Muslim.
2. List and explain the Six Articles of Faith (Arkan al-Iman).
3. Define Divine Transcendence (Tanzih) and the negative attributes (Sifat Salbiyyah) in Sunni creed.
4. Name the revealed scriptures and explain why the Noble Qur'an is the final, preserved miracle.
5. Define Ihsan and Muraqabah (mindful awareness of Allah) in daily speech and conduct.
6. Understand why Imam Malik taught that good character (Adab) precedes academic study.

---

## Section 1: The Architecture of Faith: The Hadith of Jibril
In a famous Hadith recorded in Sahih Muslim, Sayyidina 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) relates that while the companions were seated with the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, a traveler entered their gathering. He was wearing pure white garments with deep black hair. No signs of travel were visible upon him, yet none of the companions recognized him.

He knelt before the Prophet ﷺ and asked: *"O Muhammad, tell me about Iman (Faith)!"*

The Prophet ﷺ replied that **Iman has Six Pillars**:
1. **Belief in Allah**: His Oneness, absolute perfection, and freedom from all deficiencies.
2. **Belief in the Angels**: Noble beings created from light who carry out divine commands.
3. **Belief in the Revealed Scriptures**: The original books given to the messengers.
4. **Belief in the Messengers**: From Adam to the final messenger, Muhammad ﷺ. Before receiving revelation, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was known across Makkah by the title **Al-Amin** (The Trustworthy) because he never lied or betrayed a trust.
5. **Belief in the Last Day**: The Resurrection, the divine scale of deeds, and eternal life in Paradise.
6. **Belief in Divine Destiny (Al-Qadar)**: That everything in the universe unfolds by Allah's eternal knowledge, will, and wisdom.

### Adab Before Knowledge: A Golden Lesson from Imam Malik
Imam Malik ibn Anas (may Allah have mercy on him), the great scholar of Madinah, remembered that when he was young, his wise mother dressed him in student robes and said: *"Go to your teacher Rabi'ah, and learn his good manners (Adab) before learning his knowledge."* In Islam, beautiful character, humility, and respect for teachers and parents are the vessels that hold true knowledge.

---

## Section 2: Divine Transcendence (Tanzih) in Sunni Creed
In the Sunni theological tradition formulated by Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, we describe Allah with the attributes of majesty that He revealed, while upholding **Tanzih** (exalting Allah above created limits, physical shapes, or human deficiencies).

| Attribute | Arabic Term | Meaning in Sunni Creed |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Beginningless Existence** | *Al-Qidam* | Allah has always existed; there was never a point when He did not exist. |
| **Endless Permanence** | *Al-Baqa'* | Allah is eternal and will never cease to exist. |
| **Absolute Dissimilarity** | *Mukhalafah lil-Hawadith* | Allah does not resemble created things, possesses no physical body parts, and does not occupy space or change over time (Surah Ash-Shura 42:11). |
| **Self-Subsistence** | *Al-Qiyam bin-Nafs* | Allah needs neither location, physical direction, nor a creator. He is completely independent, while creation depends on Him. |

### The Consensus of the Four Sunni Imams on Transcendence
All four foundational Imams of Sunni Islam agreed upon the principle of Tanzih:
* **Imam Abu Hanifah** (d. 150 AH) wrote in *Al-Fiqh al-Absat*: Allah existed eternally before any place existed, and He is now as He ever was, without place or change.
* **Imam Malik ibn Anas** (d. 179 AH) and the scholars of creed taught that Allah created both space and time, and that Allah does not resemble anything in His creation (Surah Ash-Shura 42:11). As the scholars of creed summarized: *"Whatever comes to your mind, Allah is different from that."*
* **Imam al-Shafi'i** (d. 204 AH) and **Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal** (d. 241 AH) affirmed that Allah is exalted above limits, bodily form, and physical boundaries.

---

## Section 3: The Heavenly Scriptures & The Final Miracle
Allah sent divine revelations through Angel Jibril to guide humanity to truth, justice, and worship:
* **The Suhuf (Scrolls)**: Granted to Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham).
* **The Tawrah (Torah)**: The original scripture revealed to Prophet Musa (Moses).
* **The Zabur (Psalms)**: Revealed to Prophet Dawud (David).
* **The Injil (Gospel)**: The original scripture given to Prophet 'Isa (Jesus).
* **The Glorious Qur'an**: The final, unchangeable, perfectly preserved Speech of Allah revealed to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

While earlier communities were tasked with guarding their own scriptures, Allah took upon Himself the direct preservation of the Noble Qur'an:
> "Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur'an, and indeed, We will surely guard it." (Surah Al-Hijr 15:9)

---

## Section 4: The Concept of Ihsan: Living with God-Consciousness
When Angel Jibril asked the Prophet ﷺ: *"Tell me about Ihsan!"*, the Prophet ﷺ answered:
> "It is to worship Allah as though you see Him; and if you do not see Him, know that He surely sees you." (Sahih Muslim 8, Sahih; 40 Hadith Nawawi, Hadith 2)

* **Muraqabah (Inner Awareness)**: When you are alone in your room, you choose what is right and speak the truth because you know Allah is watching over you with complete awareness.
* **Excellence in Action**: Ihsan means performing every task with care, sincerity, and thoroughness, whether studying, helping around the house, or performing your daily prayers.

---

## Section 5: Curriculum Anchors in Practice

### 5.1 Qur'an and Tafsir Anchor: Surah Al-A'la (87:1-5)
> **سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى ۝ الَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ ۝ وَالَّذِي قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ**  
> "Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, Who created and proportioned, and Who determined and guided." (Surah Al-A'la 87:1-3)

**Tafsir Insights**: In this Surah, Allah commands us to glorify His Name above all imperfections. The name *Al-A'la* (The Most High) refers to Allah's supreme status, majesty, and power, not to a physical location in space.

### 5.2 Tajwid Rule in Action: Ghunnah and Heavy Letters
* **Ghunnah**: A nasal sound held for two counts when pronouncing a Nun or Mim with a Shaddah (`نّ`, `مّ`).
* **Heavy Letters (Huruf al-Isti'la')**: Seven Arabic letters are pronounced with a full, elevated tongue: `خ, ص, ض, غ, ط, ق, ظ`. Notice the full sound of the letter *Qaf* (`ق`) in *Al-Khaliq*.

### 5.3 Classical Text Anchor: Matn al-'Ashmawiyyah
> "The first obligation upon a morally responsible person is to know Allah, His messengers, and what has reached us of the religion." (*Matn al-'Ashmawiyyah*, Introduction).

**Explanation**: Classical Maliki manuals place understanding of faith at the very beginning of a student's education, because correct faith guides every action that follows.

### 5.4 Prophetic Hadith Anchor: Hadith 2 of An-Nawawi (Iman & Ihsan)
> "He said: 'Then tell me about Ihsan.' He replied: 'It is to worship Allah as though you see Him; and if you do not see Him, know that He sees you.'" (Sahih Muslim 8, Sahih; 40 Hadith Nawawi, Hadith 2)

**Living the Hadith**: Before starting any good action today, pause for three seconds and remind yourself that Allah sees your effort and rewards your good intention.

---

## Summary and Key Takeaways
* Iman has Six Pillars: belief in Allah, His Angels, His Books, His Messengers, the Last Day, and Divine Destiny (Qadar).
* The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was known as Al-Amin (The Trustworthy) before receiving divine revelation.
* Tanzih means recognizing that Allah does not resemble creation, has no physical body, and needs no location.
* Imam Malik emphasized that students must cultivate good manners (Adab) before seeking advanced knowledge.
* Ihsan means worshiping Allah with the deep awareness that He sees every action and intention.

# Module 1: Foundations of Belief (Level 3: Ages 10-12)

| Curriculum Metadata | Details |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Target Age Group** | Level 3: Ages 10-12 (Middle School / Pre-Adolescent) |
| **Estimated Study Time** | 50 minutes |
| **Prerequisites** | Level 2 Foundations of Belief |
| **Surah Anchor / Tafsir** | Surah Al-Buruj (85:11-22) & Surah An-Naba' (78:1-16) |
| **Tajweed Rule** | Rules of Nun Sakinah and Tanween (Izhar and Idgham) |
| **Classical Text Anchor** | Matn Ibn 'Ashir (Al-Murshid al-Mu'in, Lines 11-25) |
| **Hadith Anchor (Nawawi 40)** | Hadith 2: The Hadith of Jibril (Iman and the Intellect) |

---

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
1. Define and differentiate the Three Judgments of the Intellect (Ahkam al-'Aql): Al-Wajib, Al-Mustahil, and Al-Ja'iz.
2. Explain how the Three Judgments protect a Muslim's faith from superstition and logical confusion.
3. Formulate the Sunni concept of Divine Transcendence (Tanzih) and the attribute of Mukhalafah lil-Hawadith.
4. Distinguish between the classical Sunni interpretive approaches of Tafwid and Ta'wil when reading apparent physical descriptions.
5. Memorize and explain the foundational creed lines from Matn Ibn 'Ashir.
6. Connect the Six Articles of Faith to personal accountability, moral duty, and the stages of the Hereafter.

---

## Section 1: Building an Analytical Faith
Faith in Islam (*Iman*) is not a blind emotional wish; it is firm conviction rooted in sound rational proof illuminated by divine revelation. At ages 10 to 12, your intellect is developing the ability to analyze arguments, categorize reality, and assess claims logically.

Classical Sunni theologians, such as Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari and Imam Abu Bakr al-Baqillani, developed a logical framework known as the **Three Judgments of the Intellect** (*Ahkam al-'Aql*). Before studying specific theological texts, every student must understand how the human mind evaluates any statement:

| Judgment of the Intellect | Arabic Term | Definition | Universal Logical Example | Theological Application |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **The Rationally Necessary** | *Al-Wajib al-'Aqli* | That which the sound mind cannot conceive of as nonexistent. | The whole of an object is larger than any of its parts. | The existence of one eternal, uncreated Creator (*Wujud Allah*). |
| **The Rationally Impossible** | *Al-Mustahil al-'Aqli* | That which the sound mind cannot conceive of as existing, because it contains an internal contradiction. | A shape that is simultaneously a square and a circle at the exact same moment. | Allah having a partner, beginning, physical body, or child. |
| **The Rationally Possible** | *Al-Ja'iz al-'Aqli* | That which the sound mind can conceive of as either existing or not existing without logical contradiction. | Whether it rains tomorrow, or whether an empire rises or falls. | Allah creating humanity, sending messengers, or forgiving a repentant believer. |

Understanding these categories equips a young Muslim to answer confused questions with clarity. For instance, when a skeptic asks: *"Can Allah create a rock so heavy He cannot lift it?"*, the student knows that an omnipotent Creator being unable to do something is a self-contradictory absurdity (*Al-Mustahil al-'Aqli*). Omnipotence (*Qudrah*) relates to all possibilities (*Al-Ja'izat*), not to logical nonsense.

---

## Section 2: Divine Transcendence: Tanzih vs. Anthropomorphism
Sunni theology is distinguished by **Tanzih** (تَنْزِيه), which means affirming that Allah is completely exalted above all created limits, flaws, parts, or physical dimensions.

### The Attribute of Mukhalafah lil-Hawadith (مُخَالَفَتُهُ لِلْحَوَادِثِ)
This attribute establishes that **Allah is entirely different from created things**:
* **Creation occupies space**: Allah created space and is not contained within it.
* **Creation is subject to time**: Allah created time and does not change across seconds, hours, or centuries.
* **Creation possesses physical forms and limits**: Allah has no physical body (*Jism*), organs, or boundaries.

Imam Dhu al-Nun al-Misri and Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal formulated the famous maxim of creed:
> *"Whatever comes to your mind, Allah is completely different from that."* (*Kullu ma khatara bi-balika fa-Allahu bi-khilafi dhalik*, cited by al-Qushayri in his *Risalah*).

### Understanding Apparent Bodily Descriptions in Classical Scholarship
When verses in the Qur'an use words that could be misunderstood physically (such as *Yad* or *Wajh*), Sunni scholars approached them with reverence and strict Tanzih through two recognized paths:
1. **The Method of the Early Predecessors (Tafwid)**: Affirming the text as revealed while completely denying any physical limb, bodily shape, or created resemblance (*Bila Kayf*).
2. **The Method of Later Scholars (Ta'wil)**: Explaining the word according to classical Arabic figurative eloquence (for example, understanding *Yad* to mean divine power, generosity, or protection, and *Wajh* to mean the Divine Essence).

Both paths share complete consensus on the core principle: **Allah is not a physical body and does not resemble anything in creation (Surah Ash-Shura 42:11).**

---

## Section 3: Classical Creed in Matn Ibn 'Ashir
Imam 'Abd al-Wahid Ibn 'Ashir (d. 1040 AH) summarized the necessary attributes of Allah in his famous educational poem *Al-Murshid al-Mu'in*:

> **فَصْلٌ: يَجِبُ لِلَّهِ الْوُجُودُ وَالْقِدَمْ ۝ كَذَا الْبَقَاءُ وَالْغِنَى الْمُطْلَقُ عَمْ**  
> **وَخُلْفُهُ لِخَلْقِهِ بِلاَ مِثَالْ ۝ وَوَحْدَةُ الذَّاتِ وَوَصْفٍ وَالْفِعَالْ**  
> *"Section: It is necessary for Allah to have Existence and Beginninglessness, likewise Endlessness and Absolute Independence encompassing all. His absolute difference from His creation without resemblance, and the Oneness of His Essence, Attributes, and Actions."* (Matn Ibn 'Ashir, Lines 11-13).

---

## Section 4: The Six Articles of Faith and Moral Responsibility
At Level 3, the Six Articles of Faith guide our daily choices and moral accountability:
1. **Belief in Allah**: Worshiping Him alone with reverence, love, and hope.
2. **Belief in the Angels**: Being mindful that the recording angels (*Kiraman Katibin*) record every word and deed (Surah Qaf 50:18).
3. **Belief in the Revealed Scriptures**: Following the final preserved guidance of the Noble Qur'an.
4. **Belief in the Messengers**: Honoring all 25 prophets named in the Qur'an, especially the resolute leaders (*Ulul-'Azm*: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa, and Muhammad ﷺ).
5. **Belief in the Last Day**: Understanding the stages of the Hereafter:
   * **The Intermediate Realm (*Al-Barzakh*)**: The state of the soul between death and resurrection.
   * **The Gathering (*Al-Hashr*)**: All humanity assembled before Allah on the Day of Resurrection.
   * **The Scale (*Al-Mizan*)**: Good and evil deeds weighed with perfect divine justice.
   * **The Traverse (*Al-Sirat*)**: The pathway over which people pass according to their faith and deeds.
   * **The Intercession (*Al-Shafa'ah*)**: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ interceding by Allah's permission for believers.
6. **Belief in Divine Destiny (*Al-Qadar*)**: Trusting that everything happens by Allah's knowledge and wisdom, while using our free choice to perform good deeds.

---

## Section 5: Curriculum Anchors in Practice

### 5.1 Qur'an and Tafsir Anchor: Surah Al-Buruj (85:11-16)
> **إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْكَبِيرُ ۝ إِنَّ بَطْشَ رَبِّكَ لَشَدِيدٌ ۝ إِنَّهُ هُوَ يُبْدِئُ وَيُعِيدُ ۝ وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الْوَدُودُ ۝ ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ ۝ فَعَّالٌ لِّمَا يُرِيدُ**  
> "Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds will have gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great attainment. Indeed, the vengeance of your Lord is severe. Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats. And He is the Forgiving, the Loving, Owner of the Throne, the Glorious, Effecter of what He intends." (Surah Al-Buruj 85:11-16)

**Tafsir Insights**: Imam al-Qurtubi explains that *"Fa''alun lima yurid"* (Effecter of what He intends) shows that Allah's Will is executed throughout the cosmos without obstacle. He is *Al-Wadud* (The Loving), full of love for His righteous servants.

### 5.2 Tajwid Rule in Action: Rules of Nun Sakinah (Izhar and Idgham)
* **Izhar Halqi (Clear Pronunciation)**: When a Nun Sakinah (`نْ`) or Tanween is followed by one of the six throat letters (`ء, هـ, ع, ح, غ, خ`), the Nun is pronounced clearly without extra nasalization (e.g., *min tahtiha*).
* **Idgham (Merging)**: When followed by one of the six letters of *Yarmalun* (`ي, ر, م, ل, و, ن`), the Nun merges into the following letter:
  * With Ghunnah (2 counts): `ي, ن, م, و` (e.g., *Fa''alul-lima*).
  * Without Ghunnah: `ل, ر` (e.g., *Mir-Rabbika*).

### 5.3 Classical Text Anchor: Matn Ibn 'Ashir on Tanzih
> "His absolute difference from His creation without resemblance, and the Oneness of His Essence, Attributes, and Actions." (Matn Ibn 'Ashir, Line 13).

**Explanation**: This line teaches us that Allah's attributes (such as Knowledge, Power, and Will) do not resemble the limited knowledge, power, or will of human beings.

### 5.4 Prophetic Hadith Anchor: Hadith 2 of An-Nawawi (Iman and Conviction)
> "Tell me about Iman. He replied: 'It is to believe in Allah, His Angels, His Books, His Messengers, the Last Day, and to believe in Divine Destiny, both its good and its apparent adversity.'" (Sahih Muslim 8, Sahih; 40 Hadith Nawawi, Hadith 2)

**Living the Hadith**: When facing a difficult situation at school or home, remind yourself that Allah's decree contains hidden wisdom, and respond with patience (*Sabr*) and positive effort.

---

## Summary and Key Takeaways
* The intellect evaluates every statement into one of three categories: Necessary (*Wajib*), Impossible (*Mustahil*), or Possible (*Ja'iz*).
* Tanzih means recognizing that Allah is free from physical limits, shapes, parts, and locations.
* Classical scholars used either Tafwid or contextual Ta'wil when reading apparent bodily descriptions, while completely agreeing on Tanzih.
* Belief in the Last Day reminds us that our secret and open deeds will be weighed on the Mizan with perfect divine justice.

## Part A: Multiple Choice Questions

**1. How does classical Islamic theology define a "Rationally Necessary" (Al-Wajib al-'Aqli) judgment?**
(A) That which the sound intellect cannot possibly conceive of as nonexistent
(B) A legal obligation that carries a financial penalty if omitted
(C) A worldly occurrence that can exist or not exist equally

**2. Which of the following is an example of "Al-Mustahil al-'Aqli" (The Rationally Impossible)?**
(A) Heavy rain falling in a dry desert during winter
(B) A traveler reaching a distant destination in a single hour
(C) A geometric shape being simultaneously a perfect square and a perfect circle at the same time
(D) An ancient tree living for over a thousand years

**3. What is the fundamental meaning of the theological term "Tanzih" (تَنْزِيه) in Sunni Creed?**
(A) Reciting religious poetry before commencing ritual worship
(B) Exalting Allah above any resemblance to created things, bodily limits, parts, or defects
(C) Delaying the morning prayer until full sunrise
(D) Studying astronomical charts to determine prayer directions

**4. Which foundational maxim of creed was articulated by Imam Dhu al-Nun al-Misri and affirmed by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal?**
(A) "Knowledge is valid only when practiced in complete physical isolation."
(B) "Religious rulings must change whenever circumstances become inconvenient."
(C) "Human reason has no place in contemplating the signs of the Creator."
(D) "Whatever comes to your mind or imagination, Allah is completely different from that."

(A) Allah was lonely and required created companions to glorify Him

* Al-Mustahil al-'Aqli ─── Rationally impossible concept containing internal contradiction

(C) A worldly occurrence that can exist or not exist equally
(D) An empirical claim that requires laboratory testing to confirm

(B) A traveler reaching a distant destination in a single hour
(C) A geometric shape being simultaneously a perfect square and a perfect circle at the same time
(D) An ancient tree living for over a thousand years

**3. What is the fundamental meaning of the theological term "Tanzih" (تَنْزِيه) in Sunni Creed?**
(A) Reciting religious poetry before commencing ritual worship
(B) Exalting Allah above any resemblance to created things, bodily limits, parts, or defects
(C) Delaying the morning prayer until full sunrise

(A) Allah was lonely and required created companions to glorify Him

# Module 1: Foundations of Belief (Level 4: Ages 12-14) | Curriculum Metadata | Details | | :--- | :--- | | **Target Age Group** | Level 4: Ages 12-14 (Early High School / Adolescent) | | **Estimated Study Time** | 55 minutes | | **Prerequisites** | Level 3 Foundations of Belief | | **Surah Anchor / Tafsir** | Surah Al-Mulk (67:1-5) & Surah Al-Ikhlas (112:1-4) | | **Tajweed Rule** | Rules of Meem Sakinah (Ikhfa' Shafawi, Idgham Shafawi, Izhar Shafawi) | | **Classical Text Anchor** | Sanusi's Umm al-Barahin & Al-Risalah of Ibn Abi Zayd | | **Hadith Anchor (Nawawi 40)** | Hadith 2: The Hadith of Jibril (The 6 Articles of Iman) | --- ## Learning Objectives By the end of this lesson, you will be able to: 1. Explain the moral and legal significance of reaching Bulugh (puberty and moral accountability / Taklif). 2. Classify and articulate the 20 Necessary Attributes of Allah (Al-Sifat al-Wajibah) according to the Sanusi taxonomy. 3. Identify the 20 Impossible attributes (Al-Mustahilat) and the one Permissible attribute (Al-Ja'iz). 4. Define the four necessary attributes of the Messengers (Sidq, Amanah, Tabligh, Fatanah) and the doctrine of Prophetic Infallibility ('Ismah). 5. Compare the historical methodologies of the Ash'ari, Maturidi, and Athari schools within Ahl al-Sunnah. --- ## Section 1: The Threshold of Moral Accountability (Bulugh and Taklif) As a young Muslim enters the years of **Bulugh** (puberty and physical maturity), Islamic jurisprudence recognizes them as a morally responsible believer (*Mukallaf*). Your religious obligations are no longer childhood practice; they are personal covenants between you and Allah, recorded directly by the angels. Classical Sunni theologians, following the Qur'anic method, taught that the primary intellectual duty upon a discerning person is to attain grounded knowledge of Allah through reflective reasoning (*Ma'rifat Allah bi-Nazar*). This is not cold abstract philosophy; it means using the intellect (*'Aql*) that Allah created within you to observe the signs in the cosmos and recognize His unshared majesty, power, and mercy. --- ## Section 2: The Sanusi Framework: The 20 Necessary Attributes of Allah Imam Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Sanusi (d. 895 AH), a prominent North African Maliki scholar, organized the necessary attributes of Allah into four logical categories in his famous theological manual *Umm al-Barahin* (*The Mother of Proofs*): | Category | Count | Divine Attributes | Theological Meaning | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **1. Al-Sifah al-Nafsiyyah (Essential Attribute)** | 1 | **Al-Wujud** (Existence) | Allah exists necessarily by His own Essence, without beginning, end, or external cause. | | **2. Al-Sifat al-Salbiyyah (Negative Attributes)** | 5 | **Al-Qidam** (Pre-Eternity)
**Al-Baqa'** (Endlessness)
**Mukhalafah lil-Hawadith** (Absolute Incomparability)
**Al-Qiyam bin-Nafs** (Self-Subsistence)
**Al-Wahdaniyyah** (Absolute Oneness) | These attributes negate all deficiencies:
1. *Qidam*: He has no beginning.
2. *Baqa'*: He never ceases to exist.
3. *Mukhalafah*: He has no physical body, shape, or location (Surah Ash-Shura 42:11).
4. *Qiyam bin-Nafs*: He needs no creator, location, or supporter.
5. *Wahdaniyyah*: One in Essence, Attributes, and Actions. | | **3. Sifat al-Ma'ani (Qualitative Attributes)** | 7 | **Al-Qudrah** (Power)
**Al-Iradah** (Will)
**Al-'Ilm** (Knowledge)
**Al-Hayah** (Life)
**Al-Sam'** (Hearing)
**Al-Basar** (Sight)
**Al-Kalam** (Speech) | Eternal, living attributes subsisting with the Divine Essence:
1. *Qudrah*: Brings all possibilities into existence.
2. *Iradah*: Specifies what exists and when.
3. *'Ilm*: Encompasses everything without learning or forgetting.
4. *Hayah*: Eternal, uncreated life.
5. *Sam'*: Hears all sounds without physical ears.
6. *Basar*: Sees all existences without physical eyes.
7. *Kalam*: Divine speech without letters or vocal chords. | | **4. Sifat al-Ma'nawiyyah (Active Relational States)** | 7 | **Kaunuhu Qadiran**
**Kaunuhu Muridan**
**Kaunuhu 'Aliman**
**Kaunuhu Hayyan**
**Kaunuhu Sami'an**
**Kaunuhu Basiran**
**Kaunuhu Mutakalliman** | The active state of being eternally All-Powerful, All-Willing, All-Knowing, Living, All-Hearing, All-Seeing, and Speaking. | ### The 20 Impossible Attributes (*Al-Mustahilat*) and the Permissible (*Al-Ja'iz*) * **The 20 Impossible Attributes**: These are the direct opposites of the 20 necessary attributes. It is rationally impossible for Allah to: not exist (*'Adam*), have a beginning (*Huduth*), perish (*Fana'*), resemble creation (*Mumathalah*), need a location or cause (*Iftiqar*), have partners (*Ta'addud*), or be powerless, unwilling, ignorant, dead, deaf, blind, or unable to speak. * **The One Permissible Attribute (*Al-Ja'iz*)**: For Allah, it is permissible to create any possible thing or leave it uncreated, to send messengers, and to reward believers by His grace (*Fadl*) or hold oppressors accountable by His justice (*'Adl*). Together, these form the **41 Articles of Creed** (*'Aqa'id al-Iman*) systematized by Imam al-Sanusi to summarize the rational proofs of Tawheed. --- ## Section 3: Prophetic Infallibility ('Ismah) and the Qualities of Messengers Prophets are the human ambassadors chosen by Allah to convey divine guidance. To ensure that revelation is transmitted with absolute reliability, Sunni theology establishes four necessary attributes for all prophets: 1. **Al-Sidq (Truthfulness)**: It is impossible for a prophet to tell a lie, whether in conveying revelation or in everyday personal speech. 2. **Al-Amanah (Trustworthiness and 'Ismah)**: Complete moral protection from committing major sins (*Kaba'ir*) or public minor sins (*Sagha'ir*), both before and after receiving prophethood. 3. **Al-Tabligh (Full Conveyance)**: They delivered every single command and verse entrusted to them by Allah, concealing nothing out of fear, hardship, or social pressure. 4. **Al-Fatanah (Intellectual Acuity)**: Exceptional wisdom, clarity, and discernment, enabling them to convey truth and debate opponents with compelling reasoning. --- ## Section 4: Comparative Sunni Theology: Schools of Ahl al-Sunnah Throughout Islamic history, three main scholarly approaches developed within the broad tent of **Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah**: | School | Primary Methodology | Shared Sunni Consensus | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **The Ash'ari School** (Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, d. 324 AH) | Formulated systematic dialectical theology (*Kalam*) to defend orthodox creed against rationalist and materialist heresies. Prevalent in the Maliki, Shafi'i, and many Hanafi communities. | All three schools are united in **Tanzih**: Allah is not a physical body (*Jism*), does not occupy space, has no physical limbs, and does not resemble creation in any way (Surah Ash-Shura 42:11). | | **The Maturidi School** (Imam Abu Mansur al-Maturidi, d. 333 AH) | Parallel Sunni dialectical tradition prevalent across Central and South Asian Hanafi scholars, sharing near-identical conclusions with the Ash'aris. | | | **The Athari School** (Early Hadith scholars and Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, d. 241 AH) | Affirmed the same divine transcendence, preferring to recite textual descriptions without formal philosophical categorization, affirming *Bila Kayf* (without attributing physical form). | | --- ## Section 5: Curriculum Anchors in Practice ### 5.1 Qur'an and Tafsir Anchor: Surah Al-Mulk (67:1-3) > **تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ الْمُلْكُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ ۝ الَّذِي خَلَقَ الْمَوْتَ وَالْحَيَاةَ لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْغَفُورُ ۝ الَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ طِبَاقًا ۖ مَّا تَرَىٰ فِي خَلْقِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ مِن تَفَاوُتٍ** > "Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent, Who created death and life to test you as to which of you is best in deed, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving, Who created seven heavens in layers. You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency." (Surah Al-Mulk 67:1-3) **Tafsir Insights**: Imam Ibn Juzayy al-Kalbi explains in *Al-Tashil* that *"bi-yadihi al-Mulk"* is an Arabic eloquence signifying that absolute sovereignty and power belong solely to Allah. Notice the phrase *"best in deed"*: Allah tests the quality and sincerity of our actions, not merely their outward volume. ### 5.2 Tajwid Rule in Action: Rules of Meem Sakinah When a Meem Sakinah (`مْ`) occurs in recitation, it follows one of three clear rules: 1. **Ikhfa' Shafawi (Labial Concealment)**: When followed by the letter Ba (`ب`), the lips close lightly with a 2-count nasal Ghunnah (e.g., *tarmihim bi-hijarah*). 2. **Idgham Shafawi (Labial Merging)**: When followed by another Meem (`م`), the two Meems merge with Ghunnah (e.g., *lakum ma kasabtum*). 3. **Izhar Shafawi (Labial Clarity)**: When followed by any of the remaining 26 letters, the Meem is pronounced clearly without extra elongation. ### 5.3 Classical Text Anchor: Sanusi's Umm al-Barahin > "Know that the rationally necessary is that whose nonexistence cannot be conceived; the impossible is that whose existence cannot be conceived; and the permissible is that whose existence and nonexistence are both conceivable to the intellect." (Imam al-Sanusi, *Umm al-Barahin*). **Explanation**: This foundational definition grounds Islamic belief in clear rational evidence, liberating the human mind from superstition and blind cultural conformism. ### 5.4 Prophetic Hadith Anchor: Hadith 2 of An-Nawawi (The Pillar of Faith) > "He said: 'You have spoken the truth.' We were astonished that he asked him and confirmed him." (Sahih Muslim 8, Sahih; 40 Hadith Nawawi, Hadith 2) **Living the Hadith**: Review the 20 divine attributes with your family. Reflect on how knowing Allah is *Al-Basir* (The All-Seeing) and *Al-Sami'* (The All-Hearing) inspires honesty in private and public life. --- ## Summary and Key Takeaways * Bulugh marks the beginning of personal moral accountability (*Taklif*), where worship stems from reasoned conviction. * Imam al-Sanusi classified the 20 necessary attributes of Allah into Essential, Negative, Qualitative, and Active Relational states. * Prophetic Infallibility (*'Ismah*) guarantees that messengers are protected from major and disgraceful sins, ensuring the reliable transmission of revelation. * The Ash'ari, Maturidi, and Athari schools represent authentic expressions of Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah, united in affirming Divine Transcendence (Tanzih).

(A) Outward, Inward, Legal, and Moral

(D) Nafsiyyah, Salbiyyah, Ma'ani, and Ma'nawiyyah

(A) They describe the physical punishment awaiting oppressors in the Hereafter

(D) They list the dietary items that are ritually prohibited to consume

# Module 1: Foundations of Belief (Level 5: Ages 14-16+)

| Curriculum Metadata | Details |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Target Age Group** | Level 5: Ages 14-16+ (Senior High / Capstone Track) |
| **Estimated Study Time** | 60 minutes |
| **Prerequisites** | Level 4 Foundations of Belief |
| **Surah Anchor / Tafsir** | Surah Al-Kahf (18:1-10 & 18:65-82) |
| **Tajweed Rule** | Advanced Rules of Madd (Madd Lazim, Madd Wajib Muttasil, and Warsh Differences) |
| **Classical Text Anchor** | Jawharat al-Tawhid (Imam Ibrahim al-Laqani) & Al-Iqtisad fil-I'tiqad (Al-Ghazali) |
| **Hadith Anchor (Nawawi 40)** | Hadith 2: The Hadith of Jibril (Epistemology of Faith) |

---

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
1. Define the three foundational channels of verified knowledge (Asbab al-'Ilm) in classical Sunni epistemology.
2. Articulate and defend the logical premises of the Kalam Cosmological Argument (Dalil al-Huduth).
3. Deconstruct the philosophical dogmas of scientism, materialism, and physicalist reductionism.
4. Formulate the Ash'ari middle path of Kasb (acquisition), navigating between fatalism (Jabr) and rationalist overreach (I'tizal).
5. Provide a rigorous Islamic response to the problem of evil and worldly suffering, grounded in divine wisdom and eschatology.

---

## Section 1: Classical Epistemology: The Three Sources of Knowledge (Asbab al-'Ilm)
In contemporary academic and digital environments, young Muslims regularly encounter intellectual currents of radical skepticism, moral relativism, and physicalist reductionism. Sunni scholastic theology (*Kalam*) established a balanced epistemological framework, codified by scholars such as Imam Sa'd al-Din al-Taftazani, Imam Abu Hamid al-Ghazali, and Imam al-Sanusi.

Classical Islamic epistemology identifies **three legitimate, interconnected channels of verified knowledge**:

| Source of Knowledge | Arabic Term | Scope and Method | Examples and Validation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Sound Senses** | *Al-Hiss al-Salim* | Direct empirical observation, sensory perception, and reproducible experimental sciences. | Optics, chemistry, astronomy, biological data, and physical measurement. |
| **Sound Intellect** | *Al-'Aql al-Sarih* | Primary rational axioms, logical deduction, and mathematical truths that do not depend on sensory experiments. | The principle of non-contradiction, causality, geometry, and the three rational judgments (*Wajib, Mustahil, Ja'iz*). |
| **Veracious Report** | *Al-Khabar al-Sadiq* | Truth conveyed by infallible divine revelation (*Wahy*) and mass-transmitted, uninterrupted historical testimony (*Tawatur*). | The Noble Qur'an, verified Prophetic traditions, and foundational historical facts (such as the existence of ancient civilizations). |

### Deconstructing the Dogma of Scientism
* **Science** is an honorable, indispensable method of investigating the observable natural world through empirical inquiry (*Al-Hiss al-Salim*). Muslim polymaths, including Ibn al-Haytham in optics and al-Biruni in astronomy, laid the foundations of the modern experimental scientific method as an act of worship.
* **Scientism**, by contrast, is an unscientific philosophical assumption asserting: *"Only that which can be observed, tested, and measured in a laboratory is real or true."*
* **The Internal Self-Refutation of Scientism**: The claim *"Only empirical science gives truth"* cannot be proven by the scientific method itself. It cannot be put in a beaker, measured on a balance, or observed through a telescope. It is a metaphysical assertion that collapses under its own standard.
* Furthermore, empirical science depends entirely upon non-empirical rational foundations:
  1. The uniformity of natural physical laws.
  2. The objective validity of mathematics and immaterial logic.
  3. The reliability of human cognitive faculties.

---

## Section 2: The Kalam Cosmological Argument (Dalil al-Huduth)
Sunni theologians formulated the cosmological argument from temporal origination (*Dalil al-Huduth*), which remains at the forefront of contemporary philosophical discourse:

1. **Premise 1: Whatever begins to exist must have a cause for its existence.**  
   This rests upon the universal rational principle of causality. Something that has potential existence cannot emerge from absolute nothingness into actual existence without an external specifying agent.
2. **Premise 2: The universe began to exist.**  
   * *Philosophical Demonstration*: An actual infinite regress of past temporal moments is impossible. If the past were an infinite sequence of completed moments, time would never have arrived at the present moment, because an infinite series cannot be traversed.
   * *Physical Demonstration*: Modern astrophysics (the Standard Cosmological Model), spacetime expansion, and the Second Law of Thermodynamics (entropy) affirm that physical matter, energy, space, and time had an absolute cosmic beginning.
3. **Conclusion: Therefore, the universe has a Transcendent, Uncaused Creator.**  
   Because space, time, matter, and physical energy all originated together, their Creator must necessarily be transcendent of space, beginningless, non-physical, and endowed with supreme Power (*Qudrah*) and Will (*Iradah*). This is the Sunni affirmation of Allah.

---

## Section 3: Divine Sovereignty, Human Choice, and the Ash'ari Doctrine of Kasb
Sunni theology resolves the age-old tension between absolute divine omnipotence and human moral accountability through the doctrine of **Kasb (Acquisition)**:

| Theological Stance | Core Assertion | Inherent Flaw | Sunni Scholarly Critique |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **The Jabriyyah (Fatalists)** | Humans possess no real choice; they are like feathers blown by the wind. | Nullifies moral accountability; makes divine commands and punishment appear unjust. | Contradicts the Qur'an: "Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul" (Surah Fussilat 41:46). |
| **The Mu'tazilah (Rationalist Creatives)** | Humans independently generate and create their own actions from nothing (*Khalq*). | Posits multiple independent creators of reality alongside Allah, violating absolute Tawheed. | Contradicts the Qur'an: "And Allah created you and that which you do" (Surah As-Saffat 37:96). |
| **Ahl al-Sunnah (Ash'ari Middle Path: Kasb)** | Allah alone creates the physical power and act (*Khalq*), while the human being supplies the intentional moral choice and acquisition (*Kasb*). | None. Balances absolute divine creation with human moral responsibility. | The human is judged and rewarded or held accountable based upon the direction of their conscious moral intent (*Qasd*). |

---

## Section 4: Answering the Secular Problem of Evil and Worldly Suffering
Skeptical philosophers frequently raise the question of suffering: *"If God is All-Powerful and All-Merciful, why does suffering exist in the world?"*

Sunni theology provides a profound, multi-dimensional response:
1. **The Nature of Worldly Life as a Trial (*Dar al-Imtihan*)**:  
   This world is designed as an arena of moral testing and spiritual refinement, not as the final abode of complete peace (*Dar al-Jaza'*). As Allah declares: *"He who created death and life to test you as to which of you is best in deed"* (Surah Al-Mulk 67:2). Without challenges, virtues such as courage, sacrifice, patience (*Sabr*), and charity could not be actualized.
2. **Human Epistemic Limits and Divine Wisdom (*Al-Hikmah*)**:  
   Humans perceive only a narrow temporal fragment of reality. In the Qur'anic narrative of Prophet Musa and Al-Khidr (Surah Al-Kahf 18:65-82), events that appeared tragic in the immediate present (damaging a boat, the passing of a child) concealed protective mercy, justice, and transcendent divine wisdom.
3. **Infinite Redress in the Hereafter**:  
   In a godless, materialistic worldview, an oppressed child or a victim of cruelty receives no ultimate justice. In Islam, the Day of Judgment ensures complete redress and eternal compensation. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ explained:  
   > "The most miserable person in the world among the people of Paradise will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and dipped once into Paradise. Then it will be said to him: 'O son of Adam, did you ever see any misery? Did you ever experience any hardship?' He will reply: 'No, by Allah, my Lord! I never faced any misery, and I never saw any hardship at all!'" (Sahih Muslim 2807, Sahih).

---

## Section 5: Curriculum Anchors in Practice

### 5.1 Qur'an and Tafsir Anchor: Surah Al-Kahf (18:1-4 & 18:65-68)
> **الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَنزَلَ عَلَىٰ عَبْدِهِ الْكِتَابَ وَلَمْ يَجْعَل لَّهُ عِوَجًا ۝ قَيِّمًا لِّيُنذِرَ بَأْسًا شَدِيدًا مِّن لَّدُنْهُ وَيُبَشِّرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ الصَّالِحَاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْرًا حَسَنًا**  
> "All praise is due to Allah, who has sent down upon His Servant the Book and has not made therein any deviance. He has made it straight, to warn of severe punishment from Him and to give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward." (Surah Al-Kahf 18:1-2)

**Tafsir Insights**: Imam al-Qurtubi observes that describing the Qur'an as *"Qayyiman"* (straight and upright) emphasizes its intellectual coherence and moral guidance, standing firm against all forms of intellectual deviance and skepticism.

### 5.2 Tajwid Rule in Action: Advanced Madd & Riwayah Variations
* **Madd Lazim (Compulsory Elongation)**: Elongated for 6 full vowel counts when an original Sukun or Shaddah follows a Madd letter within the same word (e.g., *Al-Sakhkhah*, *Al-Dallin*).
* **Riwayah Awareness**: In the transmission of *Warsh 'an Nafi'* (prevalent across North and West Africa), rules of *Naql* (vowel transfer before hamzah) and *Taqleel* (slight deflection of Alif toward Ya) provide distinct oral variations while preserving the exact same revealed text.

### 5.3 Classical Text Anchor: Jawharat al-Tawhid
> "Every event originated in time has an originator; therefore, reflect and reach conviction." (Imam Ibrahim al-Laqani, *Jawharat al-Tawhid*, Line 16).

**Explanation**: This verse summarizes the obligation of intellectual reflection (*Nazar*), reminding the mature student that belief is grounded in clear rational proof.

### 5.4 Prophetic Hadith Anchor: Hadith 2 of An-Nawawi (The Coherence of Faith)
> "This was Jibril; he came to teach you your religion." (Sahih Muslim 8, Sahih; 40 Hadith Nawawi, Hadith 2)

**Living the Hadith**: Cultivate intellectual humility and dedicate regular time to learning classical Islamic knowledge from qualified scholars to safeguard your heart against contemporary doubts.

---

## Summary and Key Takeaways
* Knowledge rests upon three sound foundations: sound senses, pure reason, and veracious report.
* Scientism is a self-defeating philosophical dogma that undermines its own rational foundations.
* The Kalam Cosmological Argument establishes that the universe began to exist and necessarily requires a transcendent Creator.
* The Ash'ari doctrine of Kasb affirms human moral accountability while upholding absolute divine sovereignty.
* Worldly hardship is understood within the context of divine testing (*Imtihan*), transcendent wisdom (*Hikmah*), and infinite compensation in the Hereafter.

(D) Because human memory cannot recall ancient history

# Presentation Slides: Islamic Creed (Aqidah) & Law (Fiqh) for Teachers
**Topic:** Who is Allah? Names and Attributes, Pillars of Iman, Angels, Holy Books & Prophets, Qadar, and Foundational Islamic Literacy.
**Target Audience:** Parents / Teachers presenting to children aged 10-13.
**Perspective:** Classical Sunni Aqidah & Fiqh.

---

## Slide 1: Islamic Creed (Aqidah) & Law (Fiqh) for Teachers
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** Elegant title slide with geometric Islamic illumination and classical calligraphy. Central title: Islamic Creed (Aqidah) and Law (Fiqh). Subtitle: Foundations of Faith for Educators and Families.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Foundations of Faith: Islamic Creed (Aqidah) & Law (Fiqh)**
  * Core Themes: Tawhid, Names and Attributes, Six Pillars of Iman, Qadar and Human Choice.
  * Classical Sunni Foundations: Ash'ari Theology and Maliki Jurisprudence.
  * Target Audience: Parents and teachers guiding youth through foundational Islamic literacy.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Welcome parents and educators. Set an inspiring, serious tone for this unit.
  * Emphasize that creed forms the heart's certainty, while jurisprudence shapes daily practice.
  * Explain that our curriculum relies upon classical texts (Umm al-Barahin, Jawharat al-Tawhid, al-Murshid al-Mu'in, al-Risalah) to provide grounded scholarship.

---

## Slide 2: Introduction to Aqidah & Fiqh
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A simple, elegant title slide. Background showing a traditional manuscript design or geometric patterns. Emphasize the keywords: *Aqidah* (Creed) and *Fiqh* (Jurisprudence).
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Welcome to our Islamic Studies Journey!**
  * **Aqidah (عَقِيدَة):** The firm belief in our hearts about Allah, the Prophets, and the unseen.
  * **Fiqh (فِقْه):** The practical rules of how we worship and live our lives.
  * Why do we learn specific schools of thought (*Madhhabs*)?
    * To build deep legal and theological literacy.
    * To appreciate the rich diversity of Islamic scholarship.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Start the class by explaining that Islam is not flat or uniform in every detail of practice and sub-theology. Scholars have preserved different, valid paths.
  * Introduce the *Ash'ari* (أَشْعَرِي) school of theology and the *Maliki* (مَالِكِي) school of law. Explain that these are followed by millions of Muslims, particularly in North and West Africa, parts of the Middle East, and historically in Muslim Spain (Al-Andalus).
  * Emphasize to the students that seeing differences in how people pray (like where they place their hands) is a sign of mercy and scholarly depth, not division.

---

## Slide 3: Who is Allah? The Core Principle of Tawhid
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A starry night sky or a beautiful nature background. Central word: *Tawhid* (تَوْحِيد) in clean, prominent text.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Tawhid (تَوْحِيد):** Uncompromising belief in the Oneness of Allah.
  * Allah is *Al-Wahid* (الْوَاحِد) and *Al-Ahad* (الأَحَد) - The One, The Unique.
  * He has no partners, no parents, no children, and no equals.
  * Knowing Allah is the very first obligation (*Wajib*) for a Muslim.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Explain that *Tawhid* is the foundation of everything. In the Ash'ari school, the first obligation upon a person who reaches the age of mental maturity (*Bulugh*) is to know Allah through reason and revelation.
  * Discuss Surah al-Ikhlas (Chapter 112) as the ultimate summary of Tawhid. Highlight the word *Al-Samad* (الصَّمَد) - the Self-Sufficient Master upon whom all creation depends, while He depends on nothing.

---

## Slide 4: Knowing Allah through His Necessary Attributes (Sifat al-Wajibah)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A table or split column layout showing the Arabic terms on one side and English translations on the other.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Sifat al-Wajibah (الصِّفَات الْوَاجِبَة):** The attributes that logically must belong to Allah.
  * Ash'ari scholars identify **20 necessary attributes** divided into groups:
    1. *Nafsiyyah* (Personal): **Wujud** (Existence).
    2. *Salbiyyah* (Negative/Divesting): Attributes that deny what is impossible for Allah (e.g., having a beginning or end).
    3. *Ma'ani* (Existential/Qualitative): Power, Will, Knowledge, Life, Hearing, Sight, Speech.
    4. *Ma'nawiyyah* (Active/State): Being Powerful, Being Willful, etc.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Explain that "negative attributes" (*Salbiyyah*) do not mean "bad." They mean attributes that negate or strip away any qualities of imperfection from Allah. For example, *Qidam* (Beginninglessness) negates that Allah was created.
  * Keep it simple for younger students: Allah is alive (*Hayy*), knows everything (*'Alim*), can do all things (*Qadir*), wills everything (*Murid*), hears everything (*Sami'*), sees everything (*Basir*), and speaks (*Mutakallim*). We will explore these one by one.

---

## Slide 5: Transcending Space and Time (Mukhalafah lil-Hawadith)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** Graphic illustrating a timeline and a globe, with a barrier or indicator showing Allah is completely outside and beyond these concepts.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Mukhalafah lil-Hawadith (مُخَالَفَتُهُ لِلْحَوَادِثِ):** Absolute difference from created things.
  * Allah is not a physical body (*Jirm*). He does not occupy space.
  * Allah created space and time; therefore, He is not contained by them.
  * *"There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing."* (Surah ash-Shura, 42:11)
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * This is a cornerstone of Ash'ari theology: *Tanzih* (تَنْزِيه), which means declaring Allah free of any resemblance to His creation.
  * Explain that everything we can imagine in our minds is a creation. Since Allah is the Creator, He cannot look like, sound like, or be like anything we can imagine. 
  * If a student asks, "Where is Allah?", the teacher should explain: Allah exists without a place (*Makan*). He created "above" and "below," so He is not physically inside or limited by directions.

---

## Slide 6: The Names of Allah (Al-Asma' al-Husna)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A collage of beautiful calligraphy of some of the 99 Names, such as *Al-Khaliq* (The Creator), *Al-Rahman* (The Merciful), and *Al-Hakim* (The Wise).
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Al-Asma' al-Husna (الأَسْمَاء الْحُسْنَى):** The Most Beautiful Names of Allah.
  * The Prophet ﷺ said: *"Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one. Whoever guards/memorizes them will enter Paradise."* (Sahih al-Bukhari)
  * We use these Names to understand Allah's actions and how He cares for us.
  * Examples:
    * **Al-Ghaffar (الْغَفَّار):** The Repeatedly Forgiving.
    * **Al-Razzaq (الرَّزَّاق):** The Provider.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Emphasize that memorizing the Names is not just repeating them like a list; it means understanding their meanings and living by them.
  * Connect the Names to daily life: when we make a mistake, we call upon *Al-Ghaffar*; when we need help or food, we call upon *Al-Razzaq*; when we see the beautiful organization of the universe, we praise *Al-Hakim*.

---

## Slide 7: Ash'ari Reading of Sacred Texts: Tafwid and Ta'wil
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A scale balance showing two valid paths: *Tafwid* (leaving the meaning to Allah) and *Ta'wil* (metaphorical interpretation).
* **Slide Content:**
  * How do we understand Quranic words like the "Hand" (*Yad*) or "Face" (*Wajh*) of Allah?
  * **Option A: Tafwid (تَفْوِيض) - The Way of the Salaf (Early Scholars)**
    * We say: We believe in the word as Allah revealed it, but we do not give it a physical meaning, and we say "Allah knows best what it means."
  * **Option B: Ta'wil (تَأْوِيل) - The Way of the Khalaf (Later Scholars)**
    * We interpret the word metaphorically using proper Arabic rules.
    * *Yad* (Hand) = Power (*Qudrah*) or Favor (*Ni'mah*).
    * *Istiwa'* (Establishing over the Throne) = Domination/Control (*Istila'*).
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * This slide is crucial for theological literacy. It teaches students that the Quran contains metaphorical language.
  * Explain that both *Tafwid* and *Ta'wil* are valid, orthodox Sunni paths. They both agree on one primary rule: **Allah does not have physical body parts.** 
  * Warn against *Tashbih* (تَشْبِيه) (anthropomorphism / comparing Allah to humans) and *Tajsim* (تَجْسِيم) (giving Allah a physical body). These are rejected in Sunni Aqidah.

---

## Slide 8: The Six Pillars of Iman (Overview)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** An infographic showing six pillars supporting a beautiful structure labeled *Iman* (Faith).
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Iman (إِيمَان):** Faith or belief.
  * The Hadith of Jibril: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about Iman and replied that it is to believe in:
    1. **Allah** (اللّٰه)
    2. His **Angels** (مَلَائِكَة)
    3. His **Books** (كُتُب)
    4. His **Messengers** (رُسُل)
    5. The **Last Day** (الْيَوْم الْآخِر)
    6. **Qadar** (قَدَر) - Divine Decree, both its good and its evil.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Remind the students of the difference between *Islam* (submission/physical actions like praying and fasting) and *Iman* (internal belief/conviction of the heart).
  * Use the Hadith of Jibril as the reference point. In it, Angel Jibril came in the form of a man in white clothing to teach the Sahabah (Companions) their religion.

---

## Slide 9: Iman in Allah and His Attributes of Power, Will, and Knowledge
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** Interlocking circles or gears showing *Qudrah* (Power), *Iradah* (Will), and *'Ilm* (Knowledge) working together.
* **Slide Content:**
  * Under Ash'ari Aqidah, three key attributes explain how Allah acts in the universe:
  * **Al-'Ilm (الْعِلْم) - Divine Knowledge:**
    * Allah knows everything eternally.
    * He knows what was, is, will be, and what *could* have been.
  * **Al-Iradah (الإِرَادَة) - Divine Will:**
    * Allah chooses to make things happen in a specific way, at a specific time, with specific qualities.
  * **Al-Qudrah (الْقُدْرَة) - Divine Power:**
    * Allah brings things from non-existence into existence.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Help students understand the relationship: Allah's *'Ilm* knows that a leaf will fall from a tree at 3:00 PM. His *Iradah* wills that this specific leaf falls at 3:00 PM rather than 4:00 PM. His *Qudrah* is the power that physically makes the leaf drop.
  * Emphasize that Allah's knowledge does not change; He does not "learn" new things. His knowledge is eternal.

---

## Slide 10: Angels: Creation, Nature, and Characteristics
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** Bright light rays against a deep background. Emphasize that angels are not human-like babies with wings, but majestic creations of light.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Angels (Malā'ikah - مَلَائِكَة):** Noble creations of Allah made from light (*Nur*).
  * They do not have physical genders (they are neither male nor female).
  * They do not eat, drink, sleep, or get tired.
  * They do not possess free will in the way humans do:
    * *"They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded."* (Surah at-Tahrim, 66:6)
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Clarify common cultural misconceptions: Angels in Islam are not "people who died and got wings." They are a completely different species created before humans.
  * Discuss their size and power. For example, Jibril is described as having 600 wings, blocking the horizon.
  * Contrast them with Jinn, who are made of smokeless fire (*Marij min Nar*) and do have free will to choose between good and evil. (Iblis was a Jinn, not a fallen angel, in Sunni theology).

---

## Slide 11: The Major Angels and Their Duties
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** Four columns or cards, each representing one of the major angels with their primary responsibility listed below.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Jibril (جِبْرِيل):** The Archangel of Revelation (*Wahy*). Delivered scripture to the Prophets.
  * **Mika'il (مِيكَائِيل):** Responsible for rain, vegetation, and distributing sustenance (*Rizq*) by Allah's command.
  * **Israfil (إِسْرَافِيل):** The blower of the Trumpet (*Sur*) to signal the end of the world and the Day of Resurrection.
  * **Malik al-Mawt (مَلَكُ الْمَوْت):** The Angel of Death (often named *'Izra'il* in tradition) who extracts souls when their time ends.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Emphasize that these angels do not act independently; they are perfectly organized soldiers executing the orders of Allah.
  * Discuss how *Mika'il* is associated with mercy because rain brings life to dry land, showing Allah's care for all living things.
  * Clarify that the name *'Izra'il* is popular in Islamic literature and cultural tradition, but in the Quran, he is referred to as *Malik al-Mawt* (The Angel of Death). Both are acceptable to mention.

---

## Slide 12: The Angels Who Accompany Us
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** An illustration of a child walking, with two soft light shapes on either side representing the recording angels, and others around them for protection.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Kiraman Katibin (كِرَامًا كَاتِبِينَ) - The Honorable Recorders:**
    * Two angels sit on our shoulders to write down our deeds.
    * The angel on the right writes good deeds immediately.
    * The angel on the left writes bad deeds, but delays writing to give us time to repent (*Tawbah*).
  * **Al-Hafazah (الْحَفَظَة) - The Protectors:**
    * Guardian angels that protect us from accidents and harm, unless Allah decrees that something should happen.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * In literature, the recording angels are sometimes referred to as *Raqib* (رَقِيب - Watcher) and *'Atid* (عَتِيد - Ready). In Ash'ari theology, these are descriptions of their qualities (that they are always present and ready to record), rather than their unique names.
  * Tell the students the beautiful mercy of the left-shoulder angel: Hadith reports that when a Muslim does a bad deed, the angel on the left raises his pen for a few hours. If the person asks Allah for forgiveness, nothing is written down!

---

## Slide 13: The Holy Books (Kutub) and the Divine Speech (Kalam)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** Images representing scrolls and books. Text highlighting the names of the books and the prophets who received them.
* **Slide Content:**
  * We believe in the original scriptures sent by Allah:
    * **Suhuf (صُحُف):** Scrolls of Ibrahim (Abraham).
    * **Tawrah (تَوْرَاة):** Torah of Musa (Moses).
    * **Zabur (زَبُور):** Psalms of Dawud (David).
    * **Injil (إِنْجِيل):** Gospel of 'Isa (Jesus).
    * **Quran (قُرْآن):** Final Revelation to Muhammad ﷺ.
  * **Ash'ari Theological Distinction:**
    * **Kalam Nafsi (كَلَام نَفْسِي):** Allah's eternal, inner attribute of Speech, which has no letters, sounds, or language.
    * The physical Quran we hold, read, and hear consists of created letters and sounds that *point to* that uncreated Divine Speech.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Explain the historical context: Sunni scholars had a major debate about whether the Quran is created or uncreated. 
  * The Ash'ari school resolved this with a beautiful distinction: Allah's attribute of Speech (*Kalam*) is eternal and uncreated, just like His Knowledge. However, the Arabic words we print on paper, the sound waves created when we recite, and the ink we use are created things. We must respect the printed Quran because of what it represents: the eternal Speech of Allah.

---

## Slide 14: Prophets and Messengers (Anbiya' and Rusul)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A chain link timeline showing the continuity of Prophets from Adam to Muhammad ﷺ, emphasizing they all brought the same message of Tawhid.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Nabi (نَبِي) - Prophet:** A man chosen by Allah to receive guidance, usually following an existing law (*Shari'ah*).
  * **Rasul (رَسُول) - Messenger:** A Prophet who is given a *new* book or a new set of laws (*Shari'ah*).
  * Every *Rasul* is a *Nabi*, but not every *Nabi* is a *Rasul*.
  * Total number: Tens of thousands of Prophets were sent, but **25 are mentioned by name** in the Quran.
  * Core message: Worship Allah alone and do good deeds.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Ask students to name some of the 25 Prophets in the Quran (e.g., Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Ismail, Ishaq, Ya'qub, Yusuf, Ayub, Musa, Harun, Dawud, Sulayman, Yunus, Zakariyyah, Yahya, 'Isa, Muhammad).
  * Explain that belief in all Prophets is an all-or-nothing pillar. We cannot believe in Muhammad ﷺ but reject Musa or 'Isa; rejecting one Prophet is like rejecting all of them.

---

## Slide 15: The Infallibility of the Prophets ('Ismah)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** Icons representing clean virtues: Truth, Trust, Intelligence, and a shield representing protection from sin.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **'Ismah (عِصْمَة):** Infallibility. The protection of Prophets from committing sins.
  * Ash'ari theology states that Prophets are protected from:
    * Major sins (*Kaba'ir*).
    * Minor sins that show a lack of character or base behavior.
    * Lying or breaking promises.
  * Four necessary qualities of every Prophet:
    1. **Sidq (صِدْق):** Complete truthfulness.
    2. **Amanah (أَمَانَة):** Absolute trustworthiness.
    3. **Tabligh (تَبْلِيغ):** Delivering the message without hiding anything.
    4. **Fatanah (فَطَانَة):** Sharp intellect and wisdom.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Why must Prophets be infallible? Because they are our ultimate role models. If they committed sins (like stealing or lying), then Allah would be commanding us to follow people who do bad things, which is logically impossible for the Just Creator.
  * Sometimes the Quran describes a Prophet making a mistake (like Prophet Yunus leaving his people early). Ash'ari scholars explain that these were not *sins* but choices between two good options where they chose the less optimal one, or small slips of judgment (*Zallah*) that Allah corrected immediately to teach humanity.

---

## Slide 16: Believing in Qadar (Divine Decree)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** An image of a pen writing on a scroll, representing the *Lawh al-Mahfuz* (Preserved Tablet).
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Qadar (قَدَر):** Allah's eternal measurement and decree of all things.
  * Four aspects of Qadar (often called the stages of decree):
    1. **'Ilm (Knowledge):** Allah knows everything eternally.
    2. **Kitabah (Writing):** Allah ordered the Pen (*Al-Qalam*) to write everything that will happen in the Preserved Tablet (*Al-Lawh al-Mahfuz*).
    3. **Mashi'ah (Will):** Everything happens only if Allah wills it.
    4. **Khalq (Creation):** Allah is the sole Creator of all things, including actions.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Introduce the concept of the *Lawh al-Mahfuz* (اللَّوْح الْمَحْفُوظ). Clarify that the "writing" of the decree does not mean we are forced to do things we don't want to do. The Pen wrote what we *would choose* to do, based on Allah's eternal knowledge.
  * Explain that Qadar is a source of peace for a believer. When something bad happens that is out of our control (like a natural storm or getting sick), we know it was decreed, and we say, *Qaddarallahu wa ma sha'a fa'ala* (Allah has decreed, and what He wills, He does).

---

## Slide 17: Human Choice and the Ash'ari Concept of Kasb (Acquisition)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A user interface metaphor: Allah creates the computer system and the keyboard (Power/Creation), but the human chooses which buttons to press (Acquisition).
* **Slide Content:**
  * If Allah creates everything, who is responsible for our actions?
  * **The Ash'ari Answer: Kasb (كَسْب) - Acquisition.**
    * **Creation (Khalq):** Allah creates the ability and the physical action.
    * **Acquisition (Kasb):** The human directs their intention and choice toward that action.
  * *Example:* You decide to give charity. Allah creates the movement of your hand and the money. You "acquire" the deed because you intended and chose to do it.
  * *"For it (the soul) is what it earned (Kasabat), and against it is what it accrued."* (Surah al-Baqarah, 2:286)
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * This is one of the most famous theological debates in Islamic history.
  * Contrast the Ash'ari view with two extremes:
    1. *Jabriyyah* (Determinists): They believed humans have no choice at all, like feathers in the wind. (Rejected!)
    2. *Mu'tazilah* (Rationalists): They believed humans create their own actions independently of Allah. (Rejected!)
  * The Ash'ari middle path is *Kasb*: Allah is the only Creator of effects, but humans are responsible because they have the freedom to intend and choose.

---

## Slide 18: Qadar is Not an Excuse for Bad Choices!
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A stop sign or warning icon. Side-by-side text contrasting "Excusing choices" vs. "Taking responsibility."
* **Slide Content:**
  * **We cannot use Qadar to justify our sins!**
  * If someone steals money and says, *"It was written in my Qadar, so don't blame me!"* - this is a misuse of belief.
  * **The Law School Analogy:**
    * If you skip studying and fail an exam, you cannot blame the teacher for writing "Fail" on your report card. You made the choice to skip studying.
  * **Use Qadar for comfort in calamity, not as an excuse for laziness or sin.**
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Share the famous story of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab: A thief was brought to him and said, "I only stole because it was decreed by Allah." 'Umar replied, "And we only cut off your hand because it was decreed by Allah!" This shows that Qadar does not bypass justice or accountability.
  * Teach students that we only look at Qadar *after* something happens (to accept it with patience), never *before* it happens (as an excuse to do wrong).

---

## Slide 19: Why We Learn Schools of Thought (Madhhabs)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A map of the Muslim world showing different colors for different schools, or a tree with different branches showing unity in the trunk.
* **Slide Content:**
  * Why do different scholars have different opinions on small details?
  * **What is a Madhhab (مَذْهَب)?** A systematic method of understanding the Quran and Sunnah.
  * The four major Sunni schools of law:
    * **Hanafi** (حَنَفِي)
    * **Maliki** (مَالِكِي)
    * **Shafi'i** (شَافِعِي)
    * **Hanbali** (حَنْبَلِي)
  * They agree on 99% of the core of Islam. Their differences are in the secondary details of practice.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Explain that the founders of these schools were great Imams who loved and respected each other. Imam Shafi'i was a student of Imam Malik, and Imam Ahmad was a student of Imam Shafi'i.
  * Reiterate that having a Madhhab is like having a guide who has mapped out the mountain. It is safer to follow an expert map than trying to climb without any training.

---

## Slide 20: The Maliki Madhhab: The Practice of Madinah and Sadl
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** An illustration of a person praying with their hands resting naturally at their sides (*Sadl*), contrasted with hands folded on the chest (*Qabd*).
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Imam Malik ibn Anas (d. 179 AH):** The Imam of Madinah, the city of the Prophet ﷺ.
  * **'Amal Ahl al-Madinah (عَمَل أَهْل الْمَدِينَة):**
    * Imam Malik looked at how the children and grandchildren of the Sahabah in Madinah practiced Islam as a living proof of the Sunnah.
  * **Sadl (سَدْل) vs. Qabd (قَبْض) in Salah:**
    * **Sadl:** Praying with arms hanging naturally at the sides. This is the preferred position in fard (obligatory) prayers in the Maliki school.
    * Why? Because Imam Malik observed the people of Madinah praying this way.
    * Both Sadl and Qabd are valid Sunni practices.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Address a common point of confusion for kids: "Why does that person pray differently?" 
  * Explain that in the Maliki school, *Sadl* is the primary position because it was the continuous, public practice of the city of Madinah. If the Prophet ﷺ had ordered everyone to fold their hands, the entire city of Madinah would not have agreed on praying with their hands down. Therefore, it is a highly respected Sunnah.
  * Note: In Maliki fiqh, it is also permitted to fold hands (*Qabd*) in nafl (voluntary) prayers, but *Sadl* is preferred in fard prayers.

---

## Slide 21: More Maliki Rulings on Salah
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** Checklist format detailing specific Maliki rulings on Salah.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Recitation of the Basmalah (بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ):**
    * In the Maliki school, we do not recite the *Basmalah* aloud or silently before Al-Fatihah in the fard prayers. We start directly with *"Al-Hamdu lillahi Rabbil-'Alamin."*
  * **Making Sujud al-Sahw (Prostration of Forgetfulness):**
    * **Ba'di (بَعْدِي - After):** If you added something extra to the prayer by mistake, you make sujud *after* the Taslim.
    * **Qabli (قَبْلِي - Before):** If you missed a sunnah act in the prayer, you make sujud *before* the Taslim.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Explain that not reciting the *Basmalah* in fard prayers is another practice of the people of Madinah. Malikis believe Al-Fatihah is the start of the recitation, and the Basmalah is a separator between Surahs, not a verse of Al-Fatihah itself.
  * Introduce *Sujud al-Sahw* (سُجُود السَّهْو) simply. The distinction between *Qabli* (before Taslim for omission) and *Ba'di* (after Taslim for addition) is a beautiful, logical system unique to the Maliki school.

---

## Slide 22: Summary & Reflection
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** Summary list on the left, a thought-bubble illustration with the word "Reflection" on the right.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **What we have learned today:**
    * Allah is Unique and not like His creation (*Mukhalafah*).
    * The Six Pillars of Iman anchor our hearts.
    * Angels surround us, recording deeds and protecting us.
    * Qadar is Allah's decree, but we are responsible for our choices (*Kasb*).
    * Scholar differences, like *Sadl* in Maliki fiqh, are a mercy.
  * **Reflection Question:**
    * *How does knowing that Allah creates our physical abilities, but we choose how to use them (Kasb), change the way you think about your daily choices?*
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Conclude the lesson by asking the students to sit quietly for two minutes to think about the reflection question.
  * Invite two or three students to share their answers. Emphasize that every choice we make (e.g., helping a friend, studying, speaking kindly) is a physical movement created by Allah, but our soul is what decided to do it, and that is what Allah rewards.

---

## Slide 23: Sources & References (For Teachers)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A academic-looking bibliography slide with book covers or text styling.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Aqidah (Ash'ari School):**
    * *Al-Aqidah al-Sanusiyyah* (Umm al-Barahin) by Imam Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Sanusi.
    * *Jawharat al-Tawhid* by Imam Ibrahim al-Laqani.
  * **Fiqh (Maliki School):**
    * *Al-Muwatta* of Imam Malik ibn Anas.
    * *Matn al-'Ashmawiyyah* by Imam Abd al-Bari al-'Ashmawi.
    * *Risalah* of Imam Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani (d. 386 AH).
  * **Hadith & Creed:**
    * *Sahih al-Bukhari* & *Sahih Muslim* (Hadith of Jibril).
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Encourage parents/teachers to reference these classical texts if they want to study deeper.
  * The *Risalah* of Ibn Abi Zayd is a standard manual for Maliki fiqh and contains a beautiful introduction to Sunni/Ash'ari Aqidah, perfect for students.

## Slide 1: Islamic Creed (Aqidah) & Law (Fiqh) for Teachers
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** Elegant title slide with geometric Islamic illumination and classical calligraphy. Central title: Islamic Creed (Aqidah) and Law (Fiqh). Subtitle: Foundations of Faith for Educators and Families.
